text.p: Arrow Transportation Co on Monday said its board of directors has directed its only operating subsidiary, Arrow Transportation Co of Delaware, to file for Chapter 11 bankruptcy today.
In a statement, the company said it fully expects to emerge from the bankruptcy a stronger, more competitive operator in the bulk freight transportation industry.
The company blamed its filing on rapid fleet and geographic expansion, an unfavorable trade union agreement, intrastate deregulation and contingent liabilities that predate current management.
It was "impossible for the company to operate without some relief from those obligations," said William Stanners, chief financial officer.

Stanners also said Arrow continues to move forward with its profit improvement plan. He said the company's primary lender has been very supportive and has agreed to provide financing during the reorganization process.
Also, Arrow said management is already working with its union workers to reach a labor agreement that would allow the company to be competitive and preserve a large number of union jobs.
